clue.text: Tear-jerker shown in club

definitions.meaning: a spray of irritant used in self-defence makes the eyes stream
a heavy staff with a spiked metal head used as a weapon

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: the brand of irritant spray and the medieval spiked cudgel.

clue.text: Master is employed without proper application

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for master, as in MA
employed means used

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster is hired despite lacking any diligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Something applied wrongly or abused has not been put to its right purpose.

clue.text: Chisel to break off ice, say

definitions.meaning: to chisel is to cut or sculpt
to cut away a slice, as when sculpting ice

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean cutting: shaping with a blade and slicing off a piece.

clue.text: Star in a backwater

indicators.note: back tells us to read the river name from right to left

parts.note: the Avon is a river, a stretch of water, in crossword shorthand

explanation.surface: A celebrity is stuck living in some sleepy rural backwater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backwater' looks like one word but splits as 'back' (the turnaround signal) and 'water' (the Avon, a common English river); 'in a' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: A nova is a star that suddenly flares to great brightness.

clue.text: One taking off cap — the first in

definitions.meaning: a bottle tool that lifts off crown caps
in cricket, a batsman who starts the innings

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the two batsmen who start the innings are the first in to bat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a device for removing lids and a batsman who opens the innings.

clue.text: Sort of clue shortened with contraction in puzzle

indicators.note: shortened means the clue-direction word loses its last letter

parts.note: across is a sort of crossword clue, as opposed to down
a tic is an involuntary muscle contraction

explanation.surface: A kind of crossword hint, trimmed and squeezed into a brainteaser.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrostic is a word puzzle where initial letters spell out a word.

clue.text: Hidden supply of dough, say

indicators.note: say tells us the money word is to be spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: dough is slang for money, cash

explanation.surface: A secret stash of bread dough, as it were.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a concealed store of goods or valuables.

clue.text: Comparing notes on play in which illnesses are dealt with

definitions.text: in which illnesses are dealt with

parts.note: to consult is to confer, comparing notes
play means room to move, scope, as in a loose joint

explanation.surface: Discussing a drama that deals with sickness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' suggests a theatre piece but means slack or leeway; 'on' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's surgery office is where patients' ailments are examined and treated.

clue.text: Get the hands together to put up sort of house

parts.note: to clap is to bring the hands together
to board someone is to put them up as a lodger

explanation.surface: Applaud for building a kind of home.
explanation.definitionFit: A clapboard house is clad in overlapping horizontal timber boards.

clue.text: Secures guarantee for a third person?

definitions.meaning: the verb form used after he, she or it

explanation.definitionFit: The verb meaning to make certain, in its he/she/it form, fits both readings.

clue.text: Trainee's informed he's bound to do this

parts.note: an apprentice is a trainee; the possessive adds the S
hip means in the know, informed

explanation.surface: The young learner knows he is obliged to serve his time.
explanation.walkthrough: An apprentice was traditionally bound by indentures to serve a master for a set term.
explanation.definitionFit: The training period is served under a binding agreement, so a novice is committed to it.

clue.text: Disease of animals — one contained in bark

indicators.note: contained in places the numeral word inside the word for bark

parts.note: to bark your shin is to scrape it
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A dog's bark holding some ailment that afflicts livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bark' suggests a dog or a tree, but here it is the verb to graze the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrapie is a fatal brain disease of sheep and goats.

clue.text: Half-hearted elopers may make tracks here

indicators.note: half-hearted means half of the middle pair of letters of the eloping word is dropped

parts.note: elopers are couples who run off together, runaways

explanation.surface: Eloping lovers with cold feet might bolt from here.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of the eight-letter word for elopers is its middle pair AW; half-hearted keeps only half of that, losing one A.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft leave wheel marks as they take off and land on airport strips.

clue.text: Female sea-bird ahead of ship in Kentish port

indicators.note: ahead of puts the bird's name before the ship's letters in the answer

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
the erne is the white-tailed sea eagle
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A female seabird flies in front of a vessel near a harbour in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: SHEERNESS is a port on the Isle of Sheppey in Kent, a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheerness is a harbour town on the Kent coast at the mouth of the Medway.

clue.text: Dark old furniture left to be disposed of

indicators.note: to be disposed of says the letter for left is thrown out

parts.note: lumber is disused furniture and junk cluttering a room

explanation.surface: Gloomy antique furniture has been abandoned for clearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dark' reads as an adjective on the furniture but is the definition, a brownish pigment.
explanation.definitionFit: Umber is a dark brown earth pigment, so a deep brown shade.

clue.text: Stubby tail?

parts.note: read as a stub left at the end, a cigarette butt, but also playfully as a hound's hind part

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a cigarette butt, the short stub left after smoking.

clue.text: Tank that has its ups and downs on the home front

definitions.text: Tank that has its ups and downs on the home front

parts.words: Tank that has its ups and downs on the home front
parts.note: not a military tank but a domestic fuel store whose telescoping top rises and falls with what it holds

explanation.definitionFit: A large telescoping storage tank for town fuel supply rises and sinks as it fills and empties.

clue.text: Not exactly slim, star comes to blows when abroad

indicators.note: not exactly suggests the letters are not in their exact order but rearranged

explanation.surface: A celebrity who has put on weight gets into fights on overseas trips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blows' suggests punches but means winds; 'comes to' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: The mistral is a strong cold wind blowing down the Rhone valley in southern France.

clue.text: Building copes with all subsidence

indicators.note: building suggests the letters are assembled into a new structure

explanation.surface: A construction copes with ground sinking beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: A structural failure where something caves in and falls down.

clue.text: Gold tooth originally found in spitoon

parts.note: a cuspid is a canine tooth
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A gold tooth was first discovered in a spittoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally found in' is link material: the pieces are in reverse order of the clue. The clue prints 'spitoon' for spittoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuspidor is an American word for a receptacle to spit into.

clue.text: Palm appearing a bit feathery?

definitions.meaning: the hollow quill or shaft of a feather

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a climbing rattan tree and the barrel of a quill.

clue.text: Drunken diners could be more malicious

indicators.note: drunken suggests the letters stagger about into a new order

explanation.surface: Restaurant patrons who have had too much may turn nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Snide means sneering and spiteful, so the comparative is nastier.

clue.text: Playboy no longer available for a commission

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute pleasure-seeker
off, as a dish struck from a menu

explanation.surface: A womaniser is unavailable for an assignment.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut or share of profits paid, often illicitly, to a middleman.

clue.text: Steals some beer

definitions.meaning: a slang term for weak or cheap ale

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to pilfer and, in old slang, thin beer.

clue.text: Dissolute — certainly not tight

definitions.meaning: dissolute describes a lax, immoral way of living

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a lax moral life and something slack and unfastened.

clue.text: Humble dress for seamen

parts.note: to humble someone is to lower them
to deck is to dress or adorn

explanation.surface: Modest clothing suited to sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress' looks like a noun but is the verb to adorn.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the ratings of a ship's crew as opposed to the officers.

clue.text: The best type of letter

definitions.meaning: a typewriter typeface of twelve characters per inch

explanation.definitionFit: The word means the select group and also a small typewriter font size.

clue.text: Craft centre, in the main

parts.note: a craft is a boat, its centre the middle part, and the main is the sea

explanation.definitionFit: Midship is the middle section of a vessel's hull.

clue.text: Rider put in for eye shield right away

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: away tells us the letter for right is removed

parts.note: a visor shields the eyes

explanation.surface: A jockey seeks a replacement for goggles straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rider' suggests a jockey but means a condition added to a document.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is an added clause or condition, exactly what a stipulation is.

clue.text: Share certificate that is split

parts.note: sc. abbreviates scilicet, Latin for that is to say
to rip is to split or tear

explanation.surface: A shareholding document that has been torn in two.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrip is a provisional certificate entitling the holder to shares.

clue.text: Nearly all stand for freedom

indicators.note: nearly all means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: an easel is a painter's stand

explanation.surface: Most people back liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: Ease means freedom from pain, trouble or constraint.

clue.text: Search the internet, say, for a servant

indicators.note: say tells us to speak the browsing word, giving a same-sounding one

parts.note: to surf is to browse the web

explanation.surface: Look online for a domestic helper.
explanation.definitionFit: A serf was a feudal labourer bound to serve a lord.
